title: Under the Surface: Tracking the Artifactuality of LLM-Generated Data
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured bias in Large Language Model (LLM) generated task labels for text with subjective or controversial content, including religious themes. It specifically compared the distribution and variation of LLM-generated labels to human-generated labels to identify if LLMs under-represent minority opinions or show less diversity in judgment on religious topics.
findings: The study found that LLMs like ChatGPT exhibit less variability than humans when annotating subjective tasks with religious content. The models tend to align with consensus or majority opinions and fail to capture the diverse perspectives present in human annotations. This results in a notable discrepancy and under-representation of minority opinions concerning religious topics, which the paper identifies as a form of religion bias, possibly stemming from the underrepresentation of minorities in the models' training data.
